title: [feat] Support CSS modules @value rule (or another way to import class names from other files)
impact: 11 reactions, 4 supporting comments (one says it is the only blocker to adopting Lightning CSS); webpack css-loader and rspack support @value. Main use case here is importing another module's hashed class name to use in a local selector (`.button .spinner`), which neither CSS variables nor the `from` dashed-ident syntax cover. Earlier request #865 was closed by the maintainer: 'CSS variables are the successor to @value'.
code: src/parser.rs: parse_prelude, "value" if css_modules -> ParserError::DeprecatedCssModulesValueRule (added in #842, v1.28.0)
summary: @value is a CSS modules convention, not standard CSS. Since 1.28.0 (#842) it is a hard error in cssModules mode ('The @value rule is deprecated'); with errorRecovery it becomes a warning and the rule is dropped, so `color: primary` stays unsubstituted and imported class names get this file's hash. The maintainer has declined value substitution twice (#6 comment 2021, #865 in 2024) because it affects every property's parsing. The class-name-import use case in this issue is distinct and has no supported alternative.
repro: 659-repro.mjs (controls only). `@value button from "./button.module.css"; .button .spinner {}` with cssModules -> ERROR 'The @value rule is deprecated' (local, 1.30.0-1.33.0); errorRecovery -> warning, rule dropped, `.button` hashed as this file's class. 1.27.0 passed it through with 'Unknown at rule' warning.
evidence: repro.mjs local + 1.27.0, 1.30.0, 1.31.1-1.33.0. Maintainer comments in #6 and #865. Docs list @value as unsupported ('superseded by standard CSS variables').

fix.approach: Value substitution (`@value x: 1px` used in any property or media query) is out of scope per philosophy: it is non-standard and requires substituting raw tokens before typed parsing of every property. If anything, consider only the import form for class names (`@value a, b from './x.css'` limited to use as class selectors), which maps onto the existing composes/`from` dependency machinery; or point the class-import use case at a different syntax. Otherwise close as won't-fix referencing #865.

subcases.status: declined (#865); CSS variables with dashedIdents + `var(--x from './file.css')` are the supported alternative

subcases.case: @value imported class names used in selectors

notVerified: Whether rspack's @value support is via Lightning CSS or its own implementation.
